hints: The scores within each country are sorted from highest to lowest.
Split the first k combined scores into i from Finland and k-i from Sweden.
Binary-search i until neither excluded next score exceeds an included last score.
analogy: A cut through two sorted lists is correct when every score to its left is at least every score to its right.
example: For Finland [9,4,3], Sweden [8,6,1], and k=3, the first three are 9,8,6, so the answer is 6.
algorithm: Binary-search i in [max(0,k-n),min(n,k)], with j=k-i. Query boundary elements F[i], F[i+1], S[j], S[j+1] as needed, treating out-of-range boundaries as infinities. If F[i] is smaller than S[j+1], decrease i; if S[j] is smaller than F[i+1], increase i. Otherwise output the smaller of the last included scores, ignoring empty sides. Flush each query and final answer.
correctness: At a valid cut, the largest excluded score is below both relevant included boundary scores, so the left side contains exactly the k highest scores. Its smallest score is the kth. Each failed comparison determines which side needs more entries.
complexity: For n<=100000, O(log n) rounds, at most 4*(ceil(log2(n+1))+1)<100 queries, and O(1) space.
